instruction: Use Abaqus via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to perform a transient heat-transfer analysis of a rectangular solid block (Variant A). Use the N-mm-MPa unit system with appropriate thermal units. Part: Create a 3D Deformable Solid, Extrusion part. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (60, 18) and extrude it by 12 mm to create a block of size 60 mm x 18 mm x 12 mm. Property: Create a material named Steel. Set the density to 7.85e-9 tonne/mm^3, the thermal conductivity to 0.045 W/(mm·K), and the specific heat to 4.5e8 mJ/(tonne·K). Create a Homogeneous Solid Section and assign it to the whole block. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the block. Step: Create a Heat Transfer step named Step-Heat-A. Use transient response. Set the time period to 300 s, the initial increment to 2 s, the maximum increment to 15 s, and the maximum allowable temperature change per increment DELTMX to 10. Initial Condition and Boundary Condition: Apply an initial uniform temperature of 25 degC to the whole block. Apply a temperature boundary condition of 95 degC on the X = 0 face during Step-Heat-A. Mesh: Apply a global seed size of 4 mm. Use DC3D8 heat-transfer brick elements and generate the mesh. Job: Create a job named Job-TransientHeat-A and submit it for solving. Wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Visualization: Review the temperature field at the final time. Record the average temperature near the X = 0 heated face, the average temperature in the X approximately 5 mm band, and the final analysis time. Save: Save the model database to C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-TransientHeat-A.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\user\Desktop\Job-TransientHeat-A.odb. [Software] To start Abaqus/CAE, run `C:\SIMULIA\CAE\2025LE\win_b64\resources\install\le\launcher.bat cae` (adjust path to your install). At the start of the task, Abaqus command-line jobs should be launched through `C:\SIMULIA\Commands\abaqus.bat`.
